correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the complete labelled indegree vector yields uniform multiset arrangements. The joint inclusion probability for r specified fixed points is prod d_i/(n)_r, giving E[(F)_r]=r!e_r(d)/(n)_r. Coefficients of H_n(z)=prod_i(1+d_i z/n) converge locally uniformly to e^{qz}prod_j(1+p_j z) because the squared tail masses are uniformly at most 1/(K+1). Uniform bounds on factorial moments transfer to the full PGF and establish total-variation convergence. The variance identity and moment uniform-integrability give the iff maximum-degree Poisson criterion. Integer-profile constructions attain every parameter sequence. An exhaustive standard-library checker enumerates 50,069 maps and 637 profiles for n<=6; finite checks do not prove the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: The complete conditional fixed-point distribution under arbitrary labelled indegrees is natural for random functional digraphs. It separates macroscopic indegree hubs into Bernoulli components from a diffuse Poisson remainder, classifies every possible weak and total-variation subsequential limit, and gives a sharp necessary-and-sufficient maximum indegree condition for the classical Poisson(1) law. This is a structural theorem answering how graph-degree concentration affects loops, rather than a routine mean computation. It may serve as a conditional baseline for mapping graph statistics, although no downstream application is claimed.
